key_insight: AiScientist shows that robust autonomous long-horizon ML engineering requires both structured orchestration of multi-step research workflows and durable state continuity so progress persists across hours or days.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap in autonomous AI research for sustained, coherent execution of complex ML workflows (task understanding, environment setup, implementation, experimentation, debugging) over long time horizons where transient agents typically lose context or fail to coordinate multi-stage work.
method: Structured orchestration: hierarchical planning and workflow decomposition to coordinate multi-step research tasks end-to-end (comprehension → setup → coding → experiments → debugging).
Durable state continuity: persistent workspace, versioned checkpoints, and long-term memory that preserve context, artifacts, logs, and partial progress across sessions.
Tool and experiment automation: integrated tooling for environment provisioning, reproducible experiment execution, automated evaluation and iterative debugging driven by the orchestrator.
impact: Enables researchers and engineering teams to offload routine, long-running ML engineering work to an autonomous system, increasing throughput, reproducibility, and consistency of experimental pipelines while reducing manual context-switching and lost progress.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the staged workflow (task comprehension → environment & data setup → implementation → experiments → debugging) coordinated by a central orchestrator.
Architecture sketch: orchestrator + persistent workspace + tool integrations (code, env, CI, logs) with arrows indicating durable state flow between steps.
Timeline visualization comparing a long-horizon run with state continuity (steady progress, checkpoints) versus a baseline agent that loses context and stalls.
Bar/line chart of key metrics (task completion rate, time-to-results, reproducibility) showing AiScientist vs baseline.
paper_title: Toward Autonomous Long-Horizon Engineering for ML Research
paper_authors: Guoxin Chen, Jie Chen, Lei Chen, Jiale Zhao, Fanzhe Meng
